lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.
- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations, raising inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5% within a year.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.

- Scoring 40 vendors weekly on on-time delivery, fill rate, lead-time variance and invoice accuracy, and sharing the scorecards with buyers before each quarterly review, raised on-time inbound deliveries from 81% to 93%.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Raised on-time deliveries by 9% in simulation, from 84% to 93%, by adding customer time windows to the routing model.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Wrote a slotting guide that the volunteer coordinators used to re-slot the warehouse again after its spring expansion.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Check that the profile link works and leads to a professional profile.
Consider removing the cash and card handling detail.
items.because: It is less relevant to supply-chain roles and may take space from more relevant experience.

items.says: Consider shortening or removing the wedding-preparation and cooler-stocking duties.
items.because: They are relatively routine unless targeting retail, food, or perishables operations.

items.says: Do not present the forecast-accuracy figures as a like-for-like improvement without substantiation.
items.because: Excluding SKUs that did not sell every week changes the measurement population and may make accuracy look better without improving forecasts.

items.says: Specify whether the processing-time figures are calendar or business days.
Explain how the processing time was measured.
Clarify your contribution versus the team's contribution to the triage station.
Define what average trailer wait covers and how it was measured.
Give the period over which the wait-time reduction was measured.
Define and explain how inventory record accuracy was measured.
Make the timeframe and 2,000-location scope precise.
Specify the period used to compare the results.
Define stockouts.
Clarify what the $1.9M inventory reduction measures.
items.because: It could mean average inventory, inventory value, or another measure.

items.says: Explain the forecast approach and how the results were validated.
Check whether the freight-cost comparison accounts for fuel prices, shipment mix, volume, and service levels.
items.because: The improvement may reflect factors other than pickup consolidation.

items.says: Clarify the reorder-point method.
Add what changed as a result, if supported by evidence.
items.because: The bullet describes scope but not an outcome.

items.says: Confirm that “every SKU” is accurate.
Fix the opening grammar and tense.
items.because: “Scoring” reads inconsistently with the surrounding past-tense bullets.

items.says: Verify that scorecards were a material cause of the delivery increase.
items.because: They may have been one factor among several.

items.says: Specify the period for the 81% to 93% comparison.
The 112% OEE figure is not valid under the conventional definition.
items.because: Conventional OEE is capped at 100%.

items.says: Make the measure unambiguous if the figure is not conventional OEE.
items.because: Otherwise, it may undermine trust in the other metrics.

items.says: Confirm the claim that the team still uses the guide.
items.because: It is a durability claim.

items.says: Clarify the guide's practical contribution if there is a measurable result.
Clarify the project's scope and current status.
items.because: It began while you were at Crestway and is listed as ongoing.

items.says: Be ready to explain how you handled the project's data.
Define the baseline for the 18% reduction and reconcile it with the other routing figures.
items.because: The 18% result may use a different measure or baseline from the 120-to-90-mile result.

items.says: Clarify whether the grocer provided real data or the problem was modeled from assumptions.
Keep the modeled routing result distinct from real-world performance.
items.because: The routing results are simulated.

items.says: Calling the reduction from 120 to 90 miles 40% is incorrect.
items.because: That reduction is 25%.

items.says: Reconcile the 120-to-90-mile result with the separate 18% routing result.
items.because: The results need clearly defined, comparable baselines.

items.says: Make the on-time-delivery bullet distinct from the other time-window claim.
items.because: The time-window and on-time-delivery claims overlap.

items.says: Replace or trim the broad statement about analysis and recommendations.
items.because: It adds little beyond the project title.

items.says: Confirm that the intake-process changes were implemented.
Give a clear measured basis for the “a day sooner” claim.
Confirm whether coordinators used the slotting guide.
Clarify your role in the later re-slotting.
Show what you can do with Excel and Python using relevant tools, libraries, or techniques you have used.
items.because: The skills listing does not show what you can do with them.

items.says: Be able to explain the listed methods in enough detail.
items.because: The detail needs to support the forecasting, inventory, time-study, and routing claims.
